Where's the flash drive with the info?
Here it is.
Great.
I don't have it.
That's a pity, Marked One, a real pity. We can't talk business until you bring it to me...
Here, take it.
Good...We'll consider that you passed the test. I'd suggest you avoid going to the rookie camp.
Nothing yet.
So, did you bring the artifact?
Not yet.
Well, until you bring it, we've got nothing to talk about. Got it?
Marked One, I've told you everything already. Get outta here!
So Marked One, any news?
So, have you brought the artifact?
Yes, here it is... Damn! I've almost got torn to pieces there!!!
Yes, here it is... By the way, Sidorovich, I've spotted a helicopter nearby. It seems to have shot at somebody on the ground.
Nice job, Marked One! One more little favor and we can talk about your problem.

A heli, you say? Attacking?.. Look, Marked One, get back out there and see if you can find out who was targeted. Don't take any chances with that chopper! The military pilots don't give a shit who you are, to them everything in the Zone is hostile.
Why do you keep standing here?! Find out who got hit! Rush over there and check it out, and if it's our guys make sure you check for survivors!
Not yet, I've been scared away by a military helicopter. It seems to have attacked somebody on the ground nearby.

A heli, you say? Attacking?.. Look, Marked One, get back out there and check out who's got targeted. Don't take chances with that chopper, though! These military pilots don't give a shit who you are, to them everything in the Zone is hostile. And don't forget to pick up the artifact on your way back! C'mon, move! Maybe someone survived!
Marked One! Keep monitoring my messages next time! Here, take the medkit and go help the wounded!
I need answers to a few questions.
Ask away but I don�t know everything. I sit here all day while life goes on outside, in the Zone. I can tell you about the Zone in general and a little about the nearby areas where I've been myself.
Tell me about the Zone in general.
Ask away.
What does the army do in the Zone?

They guard and protect, what else? No one really knows whether they're guarding the Zone or protecting the rest of the world from it. Sometimes they send whole expeditions here to look for something... But I'll tell you something: they don't respect the Zone and the Zone doesn't like them either, that's why they return home in body bags very often. What else is there? Well, they look down at everyone and act like gods or something. They have no respect for stalker rules and won't ever help you even if you're dying right in front of them. They'll gladly shoot you themselves tho', and they don't get reprimanded for that... I've got a few contacts among them...you know, people always need vodka and... Umm, magazines, right? Don't annoy them - they'll whack you for nothing.
Tell me about the Zone.

The Zone... You see, it's not just a circle a few kilometers in diameter with a nuclear power plant in the center. It's something bizarre. Really bizarre. I doubt anyone in the world could give you a straight answer. I feel the Zone isn't even part of this world. It's a different, detached world, weird and dangerous... and attractive, too. And you know why? Because with a little luck anyone can get rich quick. And the closer you come to the center of the Zone, the higher you will climb on the money ladder.
What's so dangerous about this "different world"?

Hrm... Not a whole lot, except you can croak any second and not know what hit you. A dumb soldier's bullet is the least of your problems, although they've pulled in a lot of military here. Getting shot is basically the most painless kind of death in the Zone. Anomalies, now that's something for you... To die in an anomaly is a terrible thing indeed. Even mutants try to keep away from them. By the way, mutants, these "children of the Zone", are another kind of trouble, so don't go anywhere unarmed. And anyway, to learn about the other dangers, just ask other stalkers.
How does one get rich around here?

Gee, man, what do you think? You don't remember?!\n Artifacts, that's the most important thing here. All sorts of weird toys that come from the Zone are worth a fortune in the Big Land. Artifacts are more precious than gold, diamonds or pure plutonium. Why? Because no jewelry in the world can give you the supernatural powers that the artifacts possess. Just imagine: you can hang a little gadget on your belt that makes bullets swerve by and never hit you! What else? Well, you can find bits and pieces even right here. For the most valuable pieces though, you'll have to get closer to the center.
Does anyone know what's happening in the center of the Zone?

It's a different tale every time you hear it. It's a bunch of fairy tales... except I don't believe all that otherworldly nonsense. The one thing I do believe is that the center of the Zone contains a lot of valuable artifacts. Only I haven't met anyone who went there and managed to come back alive.
Do you know what happened to me?

What kind of question is that? You see, that's some shady business...\n They found you in a "death truck", that's a... a kind of corpse carrier, right? These trucks come in from the center of the Zone once in a while, loaded with bodies. No one really knows where they are heading. So, one of them crashed into something and you were found nearby. This is the most amazing thing of all. We've found broken-down corpse carriers before, but no one ever came out of them alive. I'm sorry, bro, that's all I can help you with. The rest you'll have to figure out for yourself.
Who is Strelok?

Yeah, I've heard of a stalker by that name. Rumors is he's one of the few who went to the center of the Zone and made it back. Still, we got so many of these legendary stories about stalker heroes that I can't really guarantee anything. At any rate, I've never dealt with him personally. It seems he has his own trading channels. Anyhow, just ask the folks here in the Zone and you'll be sure to learn a lot more.
Who is this Ghost stalker?
Heh, that's another local legend.\n We haven't had any news from him in a long while. I suppose he perished somewhere deep in the Zone.
What's going on in this neighborhood?

Huh! This is the entrance to the Zone, a sort of an antechamber. We've got an army cordon here. It's relatively quiet, with the exception of a couple of army guys who like to have some fun, go on shakedown runs. Experienced stalkers don't come by very often, so it's mostly rookies. Some settle here for good, yeah... A little ways from here there's a farm made into a rookie camp. Watch yourself though, they aren't afraid to pull the trigger when push comes to shove. What else? You won't make huge profit here, that's for sure. There's a deserted factory across the road. To the North, behind the railroad embankment there are the ruins of a farm. An army outpost lies to the South of here. And beware: the military left some mines in the ground. Also, there used to be a bridge in the center, but it went down somehow. That's about it, really.
Tell me more about the army outpost.

The few soldiers there have been ordered to shoot on sight, so you'd better walk around it and try not to show your ass. If you piss them off, they may call for the Spetsnaz from the further cordon. Those guys can brew up such shit that I won't have any customers for a month... I know the commander a little: he likes to take a swig as much as the next man. I'm surviving on here thanks to him.
I want to know more about the fallen bridge.

That's just a couple of minutes North of here, you'll see it right away. There used to be a bridge over the road, but then it collapsed during one of the blowouts. The army guys built a checkpoint there and don't let anyone through... but if you grease the right palm, you'll pass with no problems. In general, you don't want to show your face there too much, unless you're badly wounded or got a heavy load on you.
Got some more info about the factory?

Cross the road and you'll see a brick building - that's it. Everything worth stealing has already been stolen, just this one box is left. This is the bandits' favorite place. I don't know if they are there now, but watch out just in case. You got nothing valuable on you to take, but do you really wanna go through all that?
Tell me about the farm.
You're getting boring, you know that? It's just a farm like any other. The place used to thrive before democracy broke out.
Thanks, that's all.
I'd like to find out more.
Tell me about this place.

OK, thanks.

You're getting boring, you know that? It's just a farm like any other. The place used to thrive before democracy broke out.
I'm ok... bleeding all over though. Gimme a medkit, will ya?
Thanks, brother!
Here you are.
Thanks, friend. A little longer and I'd... I owe you one and won't forget that. I'll send a word to Wolf, he's in charge in the camp. He'll pay you back.
Now that I have rescued you, maybe you tell me your real name and what place you are from?

Whoa, seriously!? You're either greener than the local rookies, or you must've taken a real blow to the head on the way here! *sigh* Look, let me give you a big tip to remember. The Zone doesn't LIKE people who talk about themselves. So, it's just Tolik for you, and we'll leave it at that. Of course, I do have another name stated in my documents, but that's none of anybody's concern. There's this saying around here: "Whatever the Zone has bestowed you with can never be undone". A simple rule, and it applies to both fate AND nicknames. Whatever you get, you'll have to live on with that and forget what came before. That's how things have always been for us around here. One gets into the Zone with some forged documents with some other name stated there. When he finally gets past all the trigger happy jarheads with machine-guns at the cordon, he gets the baptism of fire and an all new nickname chosen by fate in the Zone. Some have been here so long they've even forgotten their real names. That ain't even such a big deal, because after all, NOBODY needs his real name in the Zone. Most never even manage to get back out, so their old name quickly becomes irrelevant anyway. And those who do go back... Well, safe to say they are no longer the person they were when they came in... You get it? So, long story short, NEVER ask anybody about his name EVER again. Oh, and especially not where he comes from. The bandits have a long reach, you know, sometimes that reach may extend beyond the borders of the Zone, to civilization, so don't be surprised if people get pissed off with questions like that.\n Anyway, sorry for the rant, you just caught me off guard is all... We're good, right? Thanks for the help again, I'll be fine from here! See you around.
Got that, I appreciate the advice. Got any tips about what type of weapons and equipment I should invest in put here?

Sure, I can help you out. The best weapon in the Zone is by all means an assault-rifle. AK is ok, but Sidorovich sometimes gets his hands on NATO rifles as well. I never had a chance to get one, but some guys admire them, like Wolf for example. Get yourself a pistol too, so that you can get rid of small pests like rodents or blind dogs. You'll remember my advice when you see a whole pack of those bitches. Later on you'll have to choose according to the situation, either a shotgun for close encounters or a marksman rifle for long range fights. Sidorovich has got nice shotguns! I've been eager to buy myself a sawn-off automatic shotgun! A remarkable thing, I'm telling you! Not too difficult to get yourself a sniper rifle as well, perfect for hunting mutants from a safe distance. Hand grenades will also pay off, of course, they can save your ass in a pinch and apply to many different situations. You can use them to flush enemies out of cover or obliterate packs of mutants. Finally, regarding equipment, you have to invest in some real protective clothing, not just against bullets but anomalies too. All those heading further into the Zone keep getting themselves outfits like the one Wolf has. Acquire an outfit like that and you can consider yourself a true stalker. Do some work for me and I may get one for you at a lower price.
I don't feel like working for anybody.

I see... Well, I'll give you a piece of advice then. Free of charge, but not free of sense. What is the most important thing in the Zone? Right you are! INFO! It's much better than a pistol or a gas mask sometimes, it can keep you away from trouble or point you towards loot. The best thing about it is that it's easy to distribute. Press a button and there it goes. That's why every stalker uses a PDA, you can receive and store information just like that. Let's say, someone gets in a difficult situation and requires help... He's in the middle of nowhere, just him and the Zone, every man for himself... So, he sends out a global SOS message with promises of information about a stash of loot nearby. Now, not only are stalkers aware of what's happening and where, but they'll be motivated to come to assistance with promises of a reward. Of course, shit happens out here all the time, and a good ending is often the exception. So, when someone expires, never pass by the opportunity to pick up his PDA and scan it for any stored info, some traders will even buy PDAs off you for a decent price, depends who's the owner. Data transfer is very simple and every PDA contains a decoder so you can simply just press a button and transfer valuable info! If you're lucky, you'll find a location of a stash or two, automatically marked on your map!
Sorry, man. Ain't got a medkit.
Search the bodies... Our guys must have had some... gotta be there somewhere.
Not too good, but I'll live. Damn, why haven't I saved up enough to buy a bulletproof vest. Takes a fool to go deep inside the Zone without one.
Oh, damn, the pain is too much... I'm dying...
You alive?
Ugh...
You alright?
Have you got anything more interesting, maybe?

More interesting? Hmm... Ok, Marked One, listen. An order has been placed recently. From the outer side of the Perimeter. The customer longs for artifacts. Stop making a wry face! Listen to the whole story first! I'm not talking about ordinary artifacts, but about those called "dummies". Have you heard of them? \nSo, a full set is wanted. I'll supply you with the list. To tell you frankly, some of these I've never even seen for myself... They are indeed quite the rarities. The few stalkers with the skill to find them would much rather prefer to keep them rather than to sell them, and that's despite the high reward offered for them. \nSo, what do you think? Are you up for the job?
Sidorovich! Have you got the slightest idea of what god-forsaken holes I will have to delve into for them?!

I do have the idea. And that is, in fact, the reason for my asking YOU to do the job. 'Cause I know you are going to go into those holes and, what's even more important to me, you are going to get OUT of them alive with the items in question! Ok, ok... No need to negotiate a higher reward. You know me - I won't make you regret the risk. I have something remarkably special for you on the line.
Come on, tell me! What's up your sleeve?

Well... Listen... \nAbout three months ago a stalker dropped by my place... You may have seen some of his kind - scorched through by the Zone, all the fight beaten out of him... So, he asked me to assist him in getting out of the Zone and he gave me all his stuff as payment!
Stop beating about the bush! Spit it out!

So impatient, aren't you! \nMost of his stuff was quickly sold out - the stuff was remarkable indeed. But I have one item still remaining - its price is too high for any of the locals. It is the outfit. A really interesting one, I've never seen anything like that before. What I know is that it has obviously undergone a few experimental upgrades. Rare components, not commonly accessible, you know? I'm not willing to let this suit go for cheap due to its value, but I am willing to let you earn it as reward for risking your neck for me!
Alright, I'll try to get the artifacts.
No way, Sidorovich. I'm not willing to stick my head in the noose even for some miracle outfit. No offense.
As you wish. It's your choice, at the end of the day.
Well, Sidorovich, sign for the package! Full set, as per the list.
Marked One! What a sight for my sore eyes! About your reward... I have fixed it a little while you've been away on the hunt, so it's almost brand new now. Here, all yours!
I'm tired of crawling through the mud. Can you arrange some transport?

Of course I can! One thing, though: don't expect it to be delivered straight to you or to pick you up. Payment will include me having to hire someone to bring it over to a safe location close-by, so if you're around he can take it straight to you. Otherwise he will park the car somewhere in proximity. If you agree with that, place your order. If not - get lost.
To Cordon.

I can arrange a little rust bucket "Goatling" for you, have it delivered to the car park for you. It has seen some use, but it's still got 4 wheels. Just for 9'000 rubles. I need the cash up front, no refunds! \nOr if that's too risky for you, feel free to take that ZAPOR by the last house... If you manage to start it, he-he!.. It'll come out cheaper for you!
Well... So be it, bring me that "rust bucket"...
Damn, quite the racket you're running! Forget about it... I'd rather just hump it on foot...
The "Goatling" is yours. Pick it up in the garage at the car factory.
To the Garbage.
To the Garbage... Aha... There's a "Moskvich", 412, and an UAZik. 8'000 and 10'000 respectively. Money - upfront, as usual!
Let it be "Moskvich"...
The "Moskvich" is yours. You'll find it at the machinery scrapyard. Maybe you can lend a hand to somebody there...
Arrange the UAZ.
Deal. It'll be standing by those ruins in front of the Duty roadblock.
On second thought, forget about it...
To the Agroprom.
So... I can have either a UAZ "Goatling" or a "Niva" delivered. For 12'000 and 11'000 rubles respectively. Or you may try to appropriate a "Moskvich" from the military... He-he-he...
Let it be the UAZik... Better be worth it...
Pick it up by the railroad tunnel. Get lost!
Arrange a "Niva".
You'll find it... On the road from the institute...
When will you finally stop robbing people, I wonder...
To the Dark Valley.
You may have a "brick" delivered there. For 15'000 only. The place is rather dangerous, you know, so the price has to reflect that, you understand.
Well, ok then...
The "brick" will be waiting for you at the gas station, opposite Borov's camp.
Whoops... I've changed my mind...
To the Bar.
To the Bar... It's going to be a "Niva". For 12'000 cash up front.
Why so much? Well, ok, arrange it, please...
Pick it up on the road, by the gas tanker.
That's too much money... Maybe another time.
To Yantar.
Very nice! I can get a "Lop-eared" over-there for you! Small and unreliable! But for 8'000 only!
Let it be the "lop-eared" then... Hope I don't regret this...
Have it! You'll see it as soon as you enter the canyon.
Actually, maybe we can try later..
No way!
Sid... Sid..oooo...rich, heeeelp...
Marked one? What the fuck?! GUARD!!! WHAT AM I PAYING YOU FOR!?
Heeeeelp...
Wait.. You can speak?? Do you... Do you still recognize me?
Yoooou... Siiid..rich...

Now I've just about seen everything. Look, head to the eggheads at Yantar. Find Sakharov. He may be of help to you. You hear me? YANTAR! SAKHAROV! HELP YOU!! Now, get out of here before someone drops you... OUTSIDE, GO!
I... tryyyy..
The stalkers are... ermm... stalking me! Can you help with the matter?
I can, but the service is not a cheap one. I can settle the matter for 20'000. Do you agree?
I do. I want the stalkers off my back.
No. I don't really care enough to fork over that much.

Sure, I do. Not for you, though. But I would be eager to hear YOUR story. About how you happened to be in the "Death truck" in the first place... \nThat's something I cannot understand. What are these trucks? Where do they come from, and more importantly, what for? Who are their "passengers" and what does this tattoo mean? I've seen many things in the Zone, but have never come across anybody with this tattoo alive. \nI happened to hear an interesting story one time... And it was told by an experienced stalker who wasn't known for bullshitting... So, he spoke about how he had lost his companion during a raid gone wrong. They were deep in the Zone when they got caught by something similar to a Blowout...

But that wasn't a Blowout, it was something else. The storyteller managed to recover after some time, but he could not see his friend anywhere! Neither dead nor alive! He was completely sure at that point that the Zone claimed his friend. \nWell, guess what! His friend turned up at the Bar a month later - in a torn up outfit, with a different weapon and a lost expression on his face... The most interesting thing was that he came to the Bar from the Swamps, but they had gotten split up in the Red Forest! The stalker could not remember how he had happened to arrive at the Swamps, nor anything before that! Sounds familiar? You can take one guess about what was on his arm.. A tattoo, just like yours!

I've been a mercenary here in the Zone for three years already, now working as a personal security guard for Sidorovich. There are plenty of desperate bastards out there willing to step on his toes and pinch his stuff, that's why he hired me. The job isn't too complicated, the food and salary are ok as well, got to deal with shit from time to time but it's pretty quiet out here for the most part.

You are not the only one to feel like shit. Everybody's stumbling around sick right about now, some even get a kind of fever. Some call these periods "Horror Time", the others refer to them more appropriately as psi-surges. All people feel awful during these storms.

First of all I try to get out into the open space because it is easier to avoid the pervasive phantoms there. Secondly, I try to think as little as possible, because it helps to ease the headache and stay alert so as to shoot down the appearing phantoms and other shit.

Nobody knows. Some claim these phantoms to be just figments of one's imagination, or vivid hallucinations. It is known that some phantoms chase only certain stalkers without hunting the others. Eggheads from Yantar say that phantoms may appear only if other people are present nearby.

We call it the psi-surge. It happens quite frequently after a Blowout. The name "psi-surge" comes for the fact that during this period a heavy strain on the human psyche is experienced. Guys start hallucinating, raving, seeing phantoms, which may even affect one's mind permanently. They say thoughts somehow trigger these phantoms to appear. The less you think, the fewer phantoms you'll see. \nThere's no other help for psi-surges but vodka. It is the only and the best cure. Do you happen to have a bottle to spare, by the way?
Yeah, that's it!
Heh! Were you born yesterday?
That's almost true, I'm telling you.

It happens quite frequently after a Blowout. Have you noticed everybody walking around all depressed and exhausted? That's it, impossible to rest during that time. Stalkers call it "Horror Time". Well, some call it "nausea"... The deeper you push into the Zone - the worse it becomes. Poor rookies suffer greatly, but eventually every stalker learns to tolerate the symptoms. You must learn to push through it, fella! \nWhat exactly it is and where it comes from - I really don't know. But it doesn't grant additional health or a good mood, that's for certain. The eggheads at the field lab at Yantar may know something about it. If you're eager to know more - go and ask them.
Well, I see. Thank you.

Your first task is to obtain the "Stone Blood" artifact. \nThere's a gorge nearby with various anomalies, and the artifact is somewhere in the center of it. Local rookies are too afraid to go for it, but you aren't one, obviously. And I'm sure you will get it! Here, take this detector, you will need it. The coordinates will be sent to you together with some info on the artifact you're hunting and the anomaly you have to fish it out from... By the way, you are not welcome in the village. They don't trust you... Neither do I, actually. Let your actions speak louder than any words. If you prove to be ok, I will vouch for you personally.
I see. Any more info?
None. Proceed with the task!
On my way...
C'mon! Go get the artifact!
So, have you brought the artifact?
Yes, here it is... Damn! I've almost got torn to pieces there!!!
Nice job, Marked One! One more little favor and we can discuss your situation.
What kind of favor?
Not yet.
We've got nothing to talk about until you bring the artifact. C'mon! Go get it!
Marked One, damn you! Why are you still here?! Haven't I told you to rush for the artifact?!
I've acquired the dynamite. Take it.
Oh! Thanks a lot, Marked One! You've done a great job. I owe you.
I was glad to help you.
Wolf, are you interested in a dynamite crate?
A dynamite crate?! Were did you happen to find it?
It doesn't matter - no more dynamite crates there anyway. Make it fast: are you interested or aren't you?
How much do you charge?
1'000 and the crate is yours.

Look, man, aren't you charging a little too much? Be reasonable and think it over. What's more profitable for me: to pay you a "grand" and buy the dynamite, or just waste you right now and acquire the crate for the price of a single cartridge?
The second method is more profitable, I guess.
That's right! And that's how I think, too. So, let me give you 500 and you hand over the explosives, I think that deal will end up better for you in the long run.
Ok, deal then.
500? That's ok for me.
Deal. Here's your money and give me my dynamite.
It was a pleasure to do business with you. See you!
How's Tolik?

He seems ok, no need to worry, you patched him up good. He has been through worse situations before and managed to survive. He's going to become a good stalker some day... Here you are, some stuff for helping him out. Thank you, Marked One.
You are welcome. Who knows, I may need help myself some day.
So, I make a little money on the side for letting some shit leak in and out of the Zone, so what? I live and let others live too, right?
Clear enough.
Hey, wise guy, do you happen to know how much my official salary is?
Not much, I guess.
Damn right! You come and try to make it on that small change for yourself. I bet you wouldn't last a year.
It's really hard to make it, indeed.
Just imagine it. For that pittance of a salary, I am expected to display enormous pride in my service, my State and my government! What a fucking joke...
So you've lost all pride in your service?

The big wigs, every single one, are up to their necks in wealth thanks to the shit they smuggle from the Zone! All this while we're stuck here, getting shot up, torn up by anomalies, irradiated to shit and eaten alive by freaks crawling out of every shrub and not seeing a single dime of those profits that the higher-ups are swimming in. You tell me, what is there to be proud of!? Why should I keep away from this kind'a business?!
Good question.
What is every soldier's primary objective in the Zone? To carry out orders and survive! It just so happens I am carrying out my orders, and I am surviving by any means necessary!
This is just your way to make it through.

Holy crap! Everywhere I look I'm surrounded by fuckin' morons, all over the place! If I have to put up with this a little while longer, I'll either fuckin' waste everybody around me, or put a bullet through my own head!..
Yeah, you're absolutely right! Plenty of morons around! See you!
You let people through for money, don't you?
Why are you so gloomy? You're letting your thinking get all melancholy, eh?
Wait, man, let me catch my breath. Some more stories are to follow.
Hey, man. What are you doing sitting here, sighing?
Hi, I don't have time to talk right now, sorry.
What's wrong? Do you need help?
Look, give me a break, will you? I'm in real trouble right now, and I don't know how long I can last. So you better go away. There's nothing you can do for me anyway.
Well, suit yourself...
Who's that poor guy sitting in the house behind the fence?
Oh, that one... You'd better not talk to him, or our people might lose respect for you.
Why? What's wrong with him?

The bastard wanted to steal from Sidorovich. He conspired with another crook, and they came up with a plan. They threw a smoke bomb into the vent of Sidorovich's bunker. He thought there was a fire and jumped out like he was scalded, and in the meantime, wearing gas masks, they stole a lot of valuable things from his closet.
Wow!

Yeah, that's how they did their dirty work... When everything became clear, I caught up with the guys who did this. Or rather one guy, the one behind the fence. The other had disappeared somewhere, along with all their loot and belongings. He was lost in the Zone, no different - good riddance to him. His accomplice's conscience kind of kicked in at the last moment and he decided to turn himself in without a fight. We did not punish him, I pitied the fool, especially since he was being manipulated by his friend from the very beginning, I noticed it long ago. But the instigator of the theft disappeared along with Sid's loot. His stock is still recovering from that blow! We questioned this jerk about his friend's whereabouts to try and get the loot back but he wasn't much help, just babbling about his friend vanishing from sight, complete disappearing act. He didn't look like he was lying but who the hell knows, in the end we banished him from our camp so he lingers around the edges trying to find safe shelter. Without any gear or weapon he'll get eaten up by the first pack of dogs he runs into out here so he literally has no choice but to stay in the safe area and dig around for scraps of food. Some of the more soft-hearted rookies sometimes leave him a can of food or drink by the fence, so he gets by. By the way, it was because of these wiseguys that Sid had to hire that merc guard of his.
I can see why he's so moody now. I'd better ask him for some details, though.
Why did you steal from the merchant?
I didn't steal anything, how many times have I told you!!! It was all Fedka, because of him I'm totally screwed now!
Are you blaming it on a friend?
No, it's not that simple! At least hear me out, please. Maybe you'll believe me.
Go ahead, tell me your version of what happened.

My former buddy Fedka, may the Zone eat him up, once suggested that I play a joke on the local merchant Sidorovich. Life here in the village is quiet, there are few dangers, the soldiers have not bothered us lately, so we just wanted to have some fun. But Fedka was up to no good, and under the guise of a joke decided to commit a crime. Unfortunately, I realized it too late...
Go on.

He suggested that we simulate a fire in Sidorovich's hiding place and, while he was running for help, wreak a little havoc in his closet. So we did just that: we threw a lighted skein of oil-soaked rags down the chimney, and when the frightened salesman jumped out, we put on gas masks and ran in. Well, we fooled around a bit, and turned over a table and a couple of cabinets, but I didn't get anything out of there. Fedka, on the other hand, managed to fill his sack with the merchant's goods and when we jumped out of the bunker, he rushed off in the direction of the bridge. I don't know why, but instead of hiding, I ran after him.
Yes, that's what you signed your sentence with.

Most likely, yes... Serves me right for acting before stopping to think. Wolf and his associates caught up to us very quickly, we didn't even manage to get very far. But Fedka... I still can't understand what happened to him.
Something out of the ordinary?

Exactly... How can I explain it? I saw it ten meters away from me. The weather was clear, visibility was good, and there were no anomalies or beasts nearby. I turned away just for a fraction of a second, and when I looked again, he was nowhere to be seen! What the hell. I certainly understand that it sounds like a fairy tale, but this is the Zone, strange shit happens here all the time. Anyway, I don't know what to say...
Yeah, that's interesting.
Look, who's that guy in the house on the edge? Why is he separated from the others?
I'm not allowed to talk about it, sorry. You'd better ask Wolf, he'll tell you.
If you're telling the truth, then you were especially unlucky. But you yourself are to blame for what happened.
I know... Stalker, I see that you are not like the others, please help me!
What can I do for you?

I can't make it out here like this for much longer. I've noticed mutants prowling about at night, each night straying closer and closer to this shack, they can see I'm apart from everyone else and they are hungry. Won't be long before one of them gets brave enough to attack me in my sleep and drag me off into the wilderness, I can't really put up much of a fight with one mag of ammo... Hunger is an issue as well, sometimes someone will leave something for me, god bless them, but it isn't enough and I can't scrounge anything up by myself - to put bluntly, won't be long before I end up dead!
Do you want me to give you food or ammo?
No, don't do that. It might cause others to lose confidence in you. I need you to help me in another way.
How?

If I had hard evidence that I didn't want to rob Sidorovich, I think that Wolf and the others would believe me and let me back into the camp. To get this evidence, you need to find my former friend Fedka, who set me up. If you could find him, or at least prove that it was solely his intention... I myself cannot do it, I'm too weak from hunger, and I'm not equipped to survive out there, I'd be dead before the day's over. Please, help me! Find Fedka!
I would help you, but where can I find this guy? You said he disappeared!

If I'm correct in my guess, there may be a way. I've heard of a few cases where stalkers simply vanished without a trace in the Zone, only to have their bodies turn up many kilometers away from the place where they disappeared. I thought it was bullshit long ago, but now I'm not so sure. Perhaps this is the same thing that happened to Fedka? If it was some kind of new anomaly, then perhaps his body did not surface very far away? You see, here in Cordon, anomalies are usually pretty weak, so the effect may apply to whatever this is. So, can you help me?
All right, I'll look for your Fedka. Just tell me the location of the place where he disappeared.

Thank you, kind stalker, you're a good man! This place is near the garbage dump north of the village. It seems to be under one of the big trees and out of sight. Good luck with the search, be careful out there!
I found your Fedka, or rather what the bloodsucker left of him. There was something interesting in his backpack. Look, isn't that his notebook?
That's his! Is there any information about me in there?
Yes, you're in luck. He wrote out his plan in details, including where he was gonna fence the loot.

That's lucky! So I'll be exonerated. Thank you, friend, I'm very grateful to you. The only catch is that they won't let me into the camp, and they might even shoot me. Take this notebook and show it to Wolf. He knew this Fedka and should recognize that this notebook is truthful.
Okay.
Wolf, I'd like you to take a look at this. Remember you told me about the burglars? I think it belonged to one of them. I found this notebook in the tunnel behind the railroad embankment.

Well, well, well... Yes, it's Fedka's notebook, I've seen it with him more than once. And his handwriting... So it turns out that he was the instigator after all? So that's how it is. Well, thank you, man, for finding out how it really went, I can see that you're an honest and fair man!
No problem... But I have one more favor to ask of you: please take the Outcast back to the camp.

All right, I will. Now it's clear that he's just an inexperienced loser, and not a thief. I'll have him taken care of, don't worry. Here, this is for you, personally, from me. One more thing: why don't you go over to the Trader, show him this information and let him know.
Okay, I'll go see him now.
I've made arrangements with Wolf, he'll take you in.

Thank you so very much, stalker!! You are living proof that there are good, honest people in the Zone. It's a pity that I can't thank you in material terms, I simply have nothing... Wait, let me tell you something, I think it will be useful to you. There was an incident not too long ago. One night we heard some shooting and explosions near the military checkpoint, and the next day we got information that it was people who wanted to get to the Zone from the outside world, and the soldiers shot them. It seems that these people managed to break through. I carefully looked through binoculars at the place where they breached the perimeter fence, and noticed someone's corpse, lying behind the fallen tree to the east of the roadblock. My point is: you can try to search him for equipment, you won't find much else here in Cordon otherwise. And the deceased may have something of value, he no longer needs it anyway... Just be careful: after this incident, the military set up more heavy machine-gun emplacements. The body is in a blind-spot where they can't see it, but you should still be careful, the whole area is mined as well.
I think it's worth checking out, thank you.
Sidorovich, why is your assortment so sparse? I thought I could buy equipment and even guns from you, but all you have is food and bandages. What do you supply the stalkers with?

Eh, Marked One... What can I tell you? I used to have a lot of interesting things, and not so long ago. And now I don't. Don't ask me why, I don't want to talk about it. If you're so interested, you can ask that creature over there in the cabin at the edge of the village.
"Creature"?
I can't call him a stalker, and I can't call him a human. Anyway, enough about that.
Hey, Sidorovich, I brought you something.
What have you got there? Better not be a waste of time!

You know that robbery you suffered some time ago? Well, I think I know who was truly responsible. Take a look at this notebook. It belonged to a rookie named Fedka who organized the whole thing. That outcast outside the camp had nothing to do with it, he was also a victim and took the blame. Wolf can confirm that.
Holy shit! So you found the bastard?! Who would've thought... Where is he now!? I'm fixing to have a long chat with that Fedka bastard!
It seems a bloodsucker has already had a chat with him about it.
Oh, yeah? Well, good riddance to him, that thief!... Wait, here he writes that he wanted to sell my stuff to some Vovan. Do you know who this guy is?
No, it's the first time I've heard of him.

Well, you've got amnesia anyway... Okay, let me check my address book. I keep a record of some of my clients, maybe there's something about him... Yeah, there's a "Vovan from the dark valley" who came to see me once... Marked One, please, check it out when you can and see if my loot is there! They took away my hard-earned stuff, the bastards, I'm virtually penniless here! Help an old trader out! Find that Vovan, take my stuff from him if it's there and bring it back to me. I'll pay you back properly!
Why not, I'll try to find it.

Glad to hear! But hurry up, or that bastard will sell out all my stuff. What are you standing around for? Go look for Vovan. I'm losing money every second because of you. And hurry up! That's my money he's taking in his pocket!
Hello, Sidorovich! Here I am, with your loot, no less!

You managed to get it? I knew I could count on you... Hold on, let me see if everything's accounted for. All right, provisions, ammo... Where's the two latest rechargeable kits? And where are the army medical kits, ten of them??? Relax, I'm just kidding! Everything of value is mostly accounted for. Thank you very much! All right, off you go.
Aren't you forgetting something, Sidorovich? This wasn't a stroll through the park, one freak almost fed me to the mutants over your loot.

You're a self-serving man, Marked One, I can see that... I thought that maybe you wanted to do this for free out kindness for all we did for you here, but whatever, I won't have it said that Sidorovich doesn't pay his workers. I won't let you go empty-handed, so here:
Hello.
What's up, stalker?
Who are you?
Nobody really, just another stalker like you. I'm one of the Seekers, you heard of us? What about you, care to tell me a little about yourself?
No, I don't really remember much of the Zone or how I came to be here. The locals say that I have the look and habits of a veteran. Maybe in a past life I was, I can't tell yet.
Just because you don't remember anything doesn't mean you don't know anything, right?
I'd like to think so. However, I'm sure the truth will reveal itself in the future.
I agree. They call me Mentor, and I'm from the Seeker faction.
I'm Marked One, nice to meet you. Wolf told me that you need help.

Tell you what, Marked One. Let me tell you about our faction first, so you can keep up with the situation and know who the main players are. We, the Seekers, are searching for a way to the Center of the Zone. Not through the Brain Scorcher, we intend to find some other way around it. Our group was, until recently, quite large by local standards. We searched for old maps, plans, documents, scouted the territory. Having accumulated enough information about places through which it was theoretically possible to pass to Pripyat, bypassing the deadly radiation, we decided to organize an expedition. It included seventeen of the most experienced stalkers, courageous and more than once tested by the Zone, all of them like-minded people. I also wanted to be among them, maybe not meeting the requirements that were set before us, but having a great desire to see with my own eyes what is out there, beyond the Radar. However, our commander decided to leave me here. After careful consideration, the expedition decided to set out. That was about a month ago.
Pretty risky business. Did they manage to get there?

No. Something inexplicable happened: two days after the seekers stopped at the Army Warehouses, communication with them was cut off and could not be resumed. Then, after some time, some of our guys were seen in different places around the Zone: in Agroprom, Garbage, and in the Dark Valley... some sightings even here in Cordon. What happened to our guys and what they got into - only the Black Stalker knows, because no one else has seen them. We contacted the Freedom trackers, but they said they hadn't seen any of them, dead or alive. It was a massive blow to our group: it effectively ceased to exist. However, our commander and I do not believe that all of the members of our expedition were killed. That is why I decided to find at least some trace of our guys and find out what happened to them.
Do you think anyone could have survived?

Yes. And I have to find them. Look, Wolf told me that you really helped out around here, so I know you're an honest guy. He also told me that you have a purpose, someone you're looking for in the Zone. I have a big favor to ask of you: if you come across any information about our guys during your wanderings in the Zone, be kind enough to report it to our group. I will give you information about our people. Do you mind helping us?
If I find any of them, I'll let you know.

Great, then let me give you some information about our guys. Here are their nicknames and a brief description. Keep in mind, if you find any really worthwhile information, our leader Yuri will thank you. Our base is in the Bar territory. Good luck, Marked One!
Thank you.
No, I don't have time.
Wolf, what did you want to tell me? I got your message when I was at the ATP.

Yes, Marked One, after you dealt with the bandits, I realized that you're not just a rookie who's lost his memory, but probably a pretty experienced stalker. My point is this: a good man needs help, and I'd like you to help him. I think it's within your power. And it's a good deal, by the way.
What kind of guy is he?

They call him Mentor. He is a veteran of the Zone, but recently he and his group had problems and need the help of experienced stalkers. Mentor is a great friend of our Sidorovich, they say that he once apparently saved his life.
Where can I find him?
He is here in the village right now. He's staying in that red, roofless house across the street. You can go up to him right now.
Okay.
I see you're an experienced stalker. Can you tell me about the way things work here? I have some memory problems and can't recall anything useful.

Okay. Let's start with the basics: you're in an Exclusion Zone, isolated from the outside world, so the laws and orders of human society... it's not that they don't apply here, they just have a different meaning, so to speak. First off, since this is such a hostile environment, your humanity and that of others is really important here, humanity is something we can understand, it is a familiarity which brings comfort in such an alien environment as this one. It is only through mutual help and assistance for our brothers that we manage to survive here. Sure, everyone is different, and every stratum of society follows its own path to survival, but regardless of their intent, they remain familiar to you through humanity. Stalkers are busy collecting gifts from the Zone and selling them through intermediaries outside the perimeter. Bandits live at the expense of stalkers, knowing that they can make a profit without risking their lives. Members of other groups, whom you may yet meet, pursue other, more idealized goals. There are also those who are almost unknown, but they are large in number, which means that, according to the laws of logic, they also have some kind of purpose. Everyone here lives for something, Marked One, and they all represent humanity. Every day they come out of their hiding places to pursue a goal. So you, too, must find your purpose, choose your path, and never forget your humanity. Those who lose their humanity, and believe me that there have been such sad cases, well, they're no better than any mutant or anomaly. They become a part of the Zone there's nothing human or relatable about them anymore, they're just another alien part of the environment.
I think I already have a goal.

I hope so, but let's not dwell on that any more. Let me tell you about the local economy. As you can see, there are two currencies here: rubles and artifacts. Artifacts, as a means of purchase and exchange for goods, have a significant advantage over money. Why so? Look at it like this: money, as you know, tends to depreciate; but the artifacts, them and their unique properties are practically eternal. Each of them is a kind of accumulator of anomalous energy, which feeds its properties and has a reserve designed for hundreds of years. This was discovered by scientists back when the very first samples of artifacts started to reach the outside world, so everyone knows it very well. Now traders are much more willing to accept artifacts as payment than rubles, they are guaranteed to be useful for far longer than any common man-made currency. There are even traders who deal exclusively in this form of strange currency, the creations of the Zone in exchange for goods and services.
I see. What else?

I want to warn you from the start: if you are lucky enough to find an artifact, don't be in a hurry to sell it off. Try to learn its properties first, run it under a dosimeter to make sure it doesn't fry you, then try to find out any other effects it may have on you. All artifacts are divided into five categories, depending on the strength of the properties that they possess. Artifacts of the first category have weakly pronounced positive properties and strongly pronounced negative ones. The artifacts of the third category are exactly the opposite, while those of the second category have practically balanced properties in terms of potential. As for the fourth category, these are extremely rare in Zone, so little is known about their properties. But it is known that they have no negative properties, which makes them particularly valuable. There is another category - Legendary Artifacts. There are only three of them, I was once told about them, but I do not remember their names. All I remember is that each of them has a very powerful positive property, and perhaps more than one.
Interesting.

Let's go on. As you can see, weapons play an important role in life here. To protect yourself from mutants or enemies, you need to have a powerful, accurate and reliable gun, I think that's pretty obvious. You'd think it would be easy to simply buy an impressive, fancy shooter from the outside, get yourself kitted out like a one man army and then enter the Zone. However, remember where the stalkers come from and why they end up here: they are mostly poor people reduced to desperation, some were fugitives who had to flee before justice found them, without a doubt they were all in a bad situation financially before they came here and had no opportunity to even equip themselves. This is why you'll find that most stalkers acquire their kit right here in the Zone. Local traders are the only ones who can help you out in this matter: they buy old weapons on the black market and from corrupt military men and sell them to stalkers at a discount. The trouble is that most of the weapons that are smuggled into the Zone are very old and worn out. All of us around here take care of our weapons, we clean and oil them as best as we can, but nothing can fix a warped barrel or a worn out spring. Only replacement parts can do that and these can often be more expensive than the gun itself. For this reason, clean and brand new guns are a real rarity in the Zone and are worth a fortune. Having a brand new shooter like that is a real sign of status, only veterans tend to carry those around. Keep in mind that due to the local conditions, most guns you find here are not going to be reliable. They're likely to perform poorly and jam at the worst moments, even more likely to happen if you don't maintain them properly. So, do take care of your gun - just like you need food and water to eat, your gun needs cleaning and oil to keep functioning.
Thank you, I'll keep that in mind.

Okay, now about the radiation. As you know, the Zone initially began as a radiological disaster area due to the Chernobyl incident in '86, and the second disaster just made it significantly worse. Anomalous energy has a tendency to do funny things to atoms, causing even ordinary elements to shift and warp, turning them into radioactive isotopes which then release ionizing radiation to try and stabilize themselves. I'm sure the eggheads at Yantar would be able to explain all the details. What it means for us is that there are a lot of places out here where the background radiation is practically off the scale for even the most advanced military dosimeters. Even if you have no dosimeter, there are signs to look out for which indicate you've stepped into a deadly radiation field. If you begin to smell ozone like in a thunderstorm, if you taste metal in your mouth, feel pins and needles in your exposed skin or start seeing glowing pinpricks in your vision, run as fast as you can in the opposite direction. Every single second of delay means years taken away from your lifespan. We're talking about radiation fields here which make the Chernobyl disaster look like a picnic. Back then, beside the melted reactor core you could get a lethal dose in about half a minute. Nowadays, radiation fields created by anomalous energy can kill you in seconds. For this reason, radiation sickness is pretty much a guarantee around here, you WILL get it at some point, so look out for the signs. If you begin vomiting and shitting violently, you feel persistent headaches and fatigue and your skin turns red, that's radiation sickness and you need to take anti-rad meds as soon as you can. If you're lucky, you can purge any contamination in your body and stop the damage from getting worse, but then you'll just have to wait and see if the damage done to your body with initial exposure was fatal or not. Radiation over here is constant, everything you eat or drink will have contamination, the air you breathe has contaminated dust, all the time you are bombarded with high energy rays, so you will be picking up a steady dose at all times. Dosimeters here are tuned so that they don't constantly beep their alarms all the time, only the lethal fields will trigger them. Radionuclides will naturally go through your body very slowly, and if you don't purge them at once with anti-rads they will saturate your bones and organs and once that happens, they stay for good. This is a death sentence in the long run, as these little buggers will continue to damage your DNA and will definitely cause cancer down the line. So, long story short, invest in a dosimeter and wear a gas mask at all times to prevent breathing in radioactive dust. You'll still have to consume the filth when eating but a few shots of vodka after a meal will guarantee you'll piss most of it out before it settles in your organs. To be absolutely sure, take an anti-rad, it will chemically bind to radionuclides and you'll sweat it all out, although that would be extremely expensive, and if you are worried about cancer, a short life and a painful death, you came to the wrong place.
Thank you for the helpful information.

One more thing. As I mentioned before, a weapon is your tool in the Zone that will help you survive. However, like any tool, you need to know how to use it properly. The better and more accurate you are at shooting, the more likely you are to come out the winner in a fight with the enemy. Remember: the shooter's position and the position of his body play an important role when shooting. The more comfortable you are and the tighter you hold the barrel, the more accurate your bullets will be on target. This is especially true for sniper weapons. Have you ever seen a sniper making a sequence of accurate shots one after the other from a standing-up position? Certainly not, because a real sniper before an accurate shot always takes a lying position or sits down low, putting his hand with the gun on the bent knee - so that the barrel doesn't move from side to side under the weight of the rifle. That's what you should do, too, if you want to shoot sniper weapons accurately. All the things I've told you here, you can find in your PDA in the Encyclopedia section. Just so you don't forget.
I'll try to remember.
Tell me where I could find at least some gear to get started.

I've got something. But first, be kind enough to help me out a little bit. Here's my issue, not long ago I found out that my old friend named Musician was killed, here in Cordon in fact. He was a stalker, may peace be with him, and to tell you the truth he wasn't a very good fighter but he was good at playing the guitar and could sing beautifully. That's why the local people loved him. Sometimes stalkers would gather around the fire in the evening after a hard hike and musician would play them a hearty song about war or even love - he knew a lot of them. Believe it or not, I've seen many times that even the most grizzled and hardcore stalkers, completely warped and burned by the Zone, had bright eyes when they listened to his music... That's the effect he had on others. He could lift you up from the deepest pit of despair.
How did he die?

They say he was killed by a gangster. That was most likely the case: the fact was that Musician had always been what you might call penniless, living only on help from the locals or from friends like me. At one time he played for money in the bar, and then went on a journey - he liked to travel, he could not sit in one place for more than a week, which is what brought him into the Zone ... And the local gangsters have something of a code: if they have nothing to take from you, then they would just put a bullet in your head and go about their business. I remember they used to just beat you up and let you go, but now they're getting really blood-thirsty. So please, try and find Musician's remains. Most likely there will be nothing left to bury, because the local beasts would have eaten the body, but at the very least bring me his guitar. There are legends about it among the stalkers, and it will be like a memory of a good man to me. I'll repay you.
I'll look for it. And where might I find his remains, approximately?
No, I can't right now.
I don't know where exactly, but most likely here at the Cordon somewhere. Just keep your eyes peeled for anything while you explore.
Here, I found Musician's guitar.

Oh, well done... God rest his soul. Listen, how can I ever thank you? Tell you what. I'd help you with weapons, but I've only got an old sub-machine gun myself, and it's damaged... But Let me lend you some other gear, like I said I would. Here's my binoculars. They're a useful piece of equipment, and they've got an IFF heads up display too, will automatically display who is and isn't friendly based on a wireless PDA signal. Take this dosimeter, too. You'll really need it.
Thank you!
Look, I found something else on his body...
What is it?
It's a disc. Some kind of "Abnormal Album." Do you know what it could be?
No, I don't. My advice to you is to take it to the bartender. He'll know what to do with it.
Okay.
Hr-hr... Hello...
Hey there, you little runt. What do you want from me?
Hr-hr! Do you know who killed that stalker?
No, who did?
Hr-hr, I killed him... Do you know why?
What the fuck did you do that for? Are you insane?
Hr-hr! I did it to eat!
Uh, wait a minute, what are you... Fuck!
Mentor, help me out. I'm in trouble.
Tell me, I'm listening.

Some crap I picked up in my backpack, I don't know where it came from! It looks like a piece of resin, and its properties are the same: it stuck to me, I can't get rid of this thing. I can feel my strength and energy draining. What do I do, tell me!
Open your backpack wide, let me take a peek... I see, this is about worst thing that could have happened to you! Tell it to me straight: were you looting?
Well, sort of, yes. How else am I supposed to get supplies? What's that got to do with it?

And that, Marked One, is because these things in the Zone are interconnected. The thing in your backpack is called the "Black Magnet" or the "Marauder's Tavro". According to legend, the Zone throws it in the backpacks of dead stalkers under the guise of ordinary artifacts as a punishment for those who too often steal from the dead. "Black magnet" takes away the owner's vitality and energy, and besides that, as you have already seen for yourself, it is very difficult to get rid of it.
Man, what am I supposed to do, walk around half-dead for the rest of my life? Should I go to a scientist?

I don't think they can help you. Listen to me: there have long been legends among stalkers about the "Black Magnet". According to one of them, to get rid of it, you need someone to take it from you voluntarily, realizing the danger of it. If you find such a person, you're saved. In the meantime, I can only sympathize with you.
Where am I going to find such a jerk? What a mess...

Don't worry, the Zone is an unusual place, and there are a lot of unusual people here, too. Besides, a veteran once told me a story over a glass of vodka that the Fractures seem to be very fond of these gizmos and even collect them... This, of course, could just be drunken ravings, but as they say, you won't know unless you try... Anyway, good luck to you, Marked One.
Thank you...
Oh, for crying out loud...
Here you are. Where's the Jumper? Don't try to deny it, I know you stole it from the scientists!

I'm not going to lie, I'll tell it like it was: yes, I took an artifact from one of them. But don't think that I did it for profit. Listen carefully: I'm in a lot of trouble right now. Me and one other person. That person is my brother and his life is in danger right now. And this artifact is the only way to save him.
What did your brother do? Did he get into debt?

Jeez, it's a long story... I came to the Zone about two years ago and since then have led the dangerous life of a stalker. When I first planned to come here, my younger brother found out about it and also wanted to join me - just like me, he is also a thrill seeker. My brother asked me to take him along, but I turned him down because he was too young. Two years have passed since then. I did not hear from home until recently, when I received a letter from my brother. He wrote me that he had joined a group of illegals who were planning to sneak into the Zone. I realized that he was determined to get what he wanted, no matter what it took... There was nothing I could do to stop him, so at the very least I decided to ensure his safety and teach him the basics of life here. To do this, I was supposed to meet him after his infiltration, but this did not happen. I waited for the group at the agreed location for about two days, but no one showed up. Only on the third day did their contact come to me and tell me that the group in its entirety had been swept up by the military.
And?

His companions foolishly opened fire first, the soldiers started shooting back... In short, bad luck. Fortunately, I was relieved to hear that apparently my brother was unharmed and was still alive! He's being held at a military checkpoint here in the Zone, awaiting extraction and sentencing for a lot of heavy charges, we're talking life in prison. Anyway, I realized that I had to act. With great difficulty, I managed to make contact with the commander of the checkpoint where my brother was held. He turned out to be a business minded man and agreed to arrange his escape to the Zone for a reward. For his personal collection, he demanded a rare artifact called Jump, and as far as I knew only the scientists in Yantar would have something like that. I went to the chief scientist, offered him all the money I had saved up over two years, a respectable sum, but he refused to sell me the artifact. So I decided to steal it. You already know the rest.
So that's how it is. Well, you did have a good reason. But what do we do now? I promised the scientists that I'd give them back the Jumper.

I understand you. Listen: this roadblock commander is a stubborn but self-serving man. Maybe you can change his mind. I already talked to him, but he won't budge. Can you go to him and change his mind, or maybe talk some sense into him? Or at least let him take the money instead of the artifact, and I'll give him everything I've got.
How am I going to get to the roadblock, the military will kill me.
I'll send out a message that you're coming on my behalf, they will let you in.
And the land mines?
You don't have to worry about them so long as you stay on the road, the mines are only planted off the beaten path. Good luck, Marked One!
Hello, Comrade Officer. I am here on business.
At ease, scumbag. What the fuck are you doing here? You gonna ask for your brother again? You don't have to bother, he's fucked anyway.
Hold on, commander, don't be too hasty. I have a business proposition for you.
Well?
What do you want in return for this stalker's freedom?

Have you lost your mind? What fucking freedom, he wounded two of my men when we took his group! Our guys would have torn him to shreds a long time ago if I'd given the go-ahead... Do you have any idea how much his freedom would be worth to you, huh?
Oh, I see you're shrewd businessman. Name your price.
What a cockroach you are, stalker! You think your pennies are enough to build me a summer house in the Mediterranean? Ha-ha! I need 1 million rubles.
How about artifacts?

No, I already made a request for a specific artifact but it's taken too long, so I'd rather have the money. I'll give you two days! If you don't bring the cash by then, I'll issue orders for a summary execution of this saboteur.
I'll get the money, don't get too excited, commander.

Listen, I went to the military at the roadblock... Their commander wants a whole million rubles for the release of your brother. He gave me a limit of two days, after which he says he'll have him executed.

Where the hell am I going to get so much? That's the trouble! Listen, help me out, will you? Lend me at least half a mil, and I'll somehow pick up the rest myself. A man is gonna get killed here, help me out!
Okay, I'll try to raise the necessary amount of money. How much money do you have now?
This is too much. This is your problem, you deal with it yourself.

Well, thank you, man! Here, I have three hundred thousand, there you go. Now all that's left to do is raise another seven hundred grand. I'll pull all my connections and acquaintances, and in the meantime, try to raise at least half a million, okay?
Okay.
Jeez, man, that's really ice cold, leaving someone to die like that! I thought you were an honest guy...
Don't talk to me about honesty here, and give me the artifact you stole!
Oh, I don't have Jumper anymore. I sold it to get money for the bribe, I just didn't know he would ask for that much. Don't be pissed, it's a noble cause.
Okay, what the hell.
You bastard!
Well, that's it. You're free now, your brother and I have paid your ransom. Come with me.
Man, I owe you one forever! I knew my brother wouldn't leave me in this shit. Come on, let's get out of here.
Comrade Captain! I brought you something!
What have you got there?
Here, as agreed: a million rubles. It's all right by the book:

Wow, I didn't expect that, you're pretty wealthy for a stalker slime-ball! All right, this isn't enough for even half of the house, but since I'm a very kind and fair man, so be it - take your brother and get out of here with him, you have five minutes to get out of my sight! You got it?! Otherwise I'll drop the both of you!
Aye, aye, Comrade Captain!
I rescued your brother from captivity. He is free.
Holy shit, man... Now I owe you my life! Here you go, your artifact, like on a silver platter. Managed to get it back for you. Give it to the scientists and tell them not to hold it against me.
I'll be sure to do so.
Wait, here's something else from me personally:
Thank you.
No, thank YOU!.
What's the matter, Sid? Why are you looking at me like that, did I do something wrong??

What's.. What's the matter!? You're asking me what you did wrong!?!? Are you taking the piss out of me!??? Oh, let's see, how about wasting a fucking MILITARY CHECKPOINT COMMANDER?!? Now the military are going to kick up such an ungodly shitstorm of retribution around here that I won't be able to do business for MONTHS, if at all!!! Years of careful planning and cooperation, GONE! An agreeable contact within the military to facilitate smuggling and trafficking operations, DEAD! Entire platoons of pissed off Spetsnaz and jarheads patrolling all the roads and roughing up at gunpoint every lousy, flea ridden loner they come across, GUARANTEED! We're all fucked here, all because of you and your lack of trigger discipline!!! The military will leave no stone unturned!! They will waste anyone and everyone just for fun, and torture those who survive... Not to mention that I've been completely cut off from my influx of imported goods, guns, services, and my capability of getting artifacts and people out through the border is at an end. Let me guess, you came over to trade with me, yes?!
Look, I...

That's it, Marked One, I'm not going to waste my time on you, I have a business to salvage here. You won't get anything else from me: no gear, no ammo, no cars, no repairs. You no longer exist to me as far as I'm concerned, and don't be surprised if stalkers out there want you gone as well. You can go and rot out in the Zone, for all I care. I hope you catch a bullet to the gut from the military squads which are already undoubtedly mobilizing for a retaliation! Good riddance, and don't dare show your face here again!! GET THE FUCK OUT!!!!
How about we team up, I need to get deeper into the Zone. Let me tag along with you to wherever you're going.
All right, but for that I'll charge you a pseudo-dog's tail. Or five thousand rubles. Take your pick.
Take the tail.
Here's the money.
No, changed my mind.
